newsitem.title: CHINA: China leaders willing to go to Taiwan - president.
newsitem.headline: China leaders willing to go to Taiwan - president.

text.p: China's leaders are willing to travel to Taiwan, Chinese President Jiang Zemin was quoted as saying on Friday, but he urged the island to abandon attempts to break out of its diplomatic isolation.
"We are...willing to accept an invitation from the Taiwan side to go to Taiwan," the official Xinhua news agency quoted Jiang as telling the French newspaper Le Figaro.
Jiang said Taipei should prove it was sincere in its desire for senior-level talks by ending efforts to raise its international profile and climb out of its isolation.
China has considered Taiwan a renegade province that is not entitled to international recognition since their civil war ended in 1949.
"If the Taiwan authorities are indeed sincere about holding meetings, they should give up their political plot of creating 'two Chinas' or 'one-China, one-Taiwan'," Jiang said.
"Two Chinas" and "one-China, one-Taiwan" are euphemisms used by Beijing to describe attempts by the wealthy but diplomatically isolated island to raise its profile.
Meanwhile, Taiwan Foreign Minister John Chang flew to Malaysia on Friday, a day after he returned from a secretive trip to Indonesia, Malaysian state television reported.
